pockets.name: Mosskin Meadow
pockets.design_note: Open grass, few trees: passive Mosskin to learn movement and the basic attack loop. ~25 cells per mob so new players are never surrounded.

pockets.name: Sporeling Grove
pockets.design_note: Damp ground by the pond. Assist behaviour: hitting one pulls its neighbours, the first 'pack'.

pockets.name: Amber Rise
pockets.design_note: Beside the road east: assisting Sporelings cluster under the resin trees, so one stray hit from the road pulls the cluster; path around or pull deliberately.

pockets.name: Old Irrigation Ruins
pockets.design_note: Walls make chokepoints: herd passive Mosskin through a gap and AoE them. Construct prototype planned here once art exists.

pockets.name: Resin Thicket
pockets.design_note: Dense aggressive mites under resin trees: a ready-made 30-mob train for players who just unlocked Iron Cyclone at Lv5.

pockets.name: Glider Hollow
pockets.design_note: Lunari flee when hit; the hollow is ringed by forest so fleeing gliders bunch against the trees for a clean AoE.

pockets.name: Crag Outcrop
pockets.design_note: Rock-strewn ground splits the aggressive mites into small packs that pour out of the gaps; walk in carelessly and the whole outcrop comes to you.

pockets.name: Trailside Grove
pockets.design_note: Mixed aggressive + fleeing: an aggressive pack drags fleeing gliders along, a small lesson in mixed AI.

pockets.name: Cliffside Run
pockets.design_note: Wide-open grass bounded by the east cliff: assisting Craglets answer each other's calls, so a pull here becomes a slow wall of bruisers backed against the cliff face.

pockets.name: Scree Slope
pockets.design_note: Main Craglet farm at the low end of the band; rocks break line so packs come in waves.

pockets.name: Bramble Ridge
pockets.design_note: Thornback at the top of the band (Lv8): the step-up before Old Windmill.

pockets.name: Rune Circle
pockets.design_note: Standing stones split a mixed bruiser pack; good practice for cone skills through gaps.

pockets.name: Bramble Fields
pockets.design_note: Aggressive Dustwings over the fenced pasture: the fence funnels a diving swarm through the gate into one tight train.

pockets.name: Sail Hill
pockets.design_note: The signature horde: 40 aggressive, fast Dustwings that will happily form a 30-60 train. Respawn is quick so the hill refills between trains.

pockets.name: Gear Yard
pockets.design_note: Scrap piles break the ground into lanes; Dustwing packs dive down each lane at once.

pockets.name: Millrace
pockets.design_note: Dustwings hunting over the channel by the waterwheel: the water splits the pocket, so trains have to loop round it.

pockets.name: Brookbed
pockets.design_note: Passive Brookfin on the east bank: gather them with Anchor Shout (unlocked Lv8) for the first deliberate taunt-pull.

pockets.name: Reed Marsh
pockets.design_note: Aggressive ranged Reedstalkers among marsh pools: players learn to break line of sight and pull them into melee.

pockets.name: Moonlit Banks
pockets.design_note: Mixed passive + ranged: the region's most efficient pack if pulled correctly.

pockets.name: Dust Flats
pockets.design_note: Passive Brookfin sunning on the dry southern flats: a quiet, easy gather for under-levelled arrivals.

pockets.name: Rotting Rows
pockets.design_note: Slow, dense Rotroot in tree rows: rows channel a 40-60 train into lines for Meridian-style line skills.

pockets.name: Irrigation Ditch
pockets.design_note: Rotroot strung out across water channels: the channels cut a slow horde into short lines.

pockets.name: Collapsed Greenhouse
pockets.design_note: Aggressive Rotroot among broken walls; pull them through a gap for a tight AoE.

pockets.name: Old Pump House
pockets.design_note: Rotroot packed thickest round the leaking pump: a small, dense pocket and a taste of the rot that feeds from Hollowroot below.

pockets.name: Root Tunnels
pockets.design_note: The largest Barkwarden patrol in the region, in a cavern you can circle; assist behaviour brings them in as one wall.

pockets.name: Pump Hall
pockets.design_note: Construct hall at the cap level; assist behaviour means one pull is the whole hall.

pockets.name: Root Burrows
pockets.design_note: Barkwarden side cavern, a quieter construct farm.

pockets.name: Heart Chamber
pockets.design_note: Region boss, 5-7 minute respawn.

pockets.name: Fern Hollow
pockets.design_note: Passive Graftlings on open fern floor at the bottom of the band, a short walk from camp: ~21 cells each, room to gather a 40-herd with Anchor Shout.

pockets.name: Sap Grove
pockets.design_note: Tapped trunks in the north-east, beside the road to Mossbridge: passive Graftlings rooting round the taps, a safe 30-herd on the way north.

pockets.name: Glimmer Run
pockets.design_note: Graftlings on the banks of the stream and pond (the water takes ~16% of the rect); passive, so the banks are a slow, safe herd to gather along the water.

pockets.name: Grafted Ruins
pockets.design_note: Gear ruins and rune stones break the yard into lanes; passive Graftlings wander where they were first bolted together, a herd that has to be gathered round obstacles.

pockets.name: Newt Shallows
pockets.design_note: The main Newt bank, on the south shore at the bottom of the band. Banks are long and thin, so assist pulls string out along the water into a line.

pockets.name: Bridge Hives
pockets.design_note: North of the creek between the two bridges: an aggressive drone cloud mid-band that players cross on the way to Canopy Steps.

pockets.name: Mossfield
pockets.design_note: A quieter Newt bank by the obelisk, looser than the Shallows: small assist pulls for players arriving at the bottom of the band.

pockets.name: Drone Rise
pockets.design_note: Lv20 drones mid-band on the slope under the canopy, kept off the main road: a second aggressive cloud away from the bridge traffic.

pockets.name: Barkhound Den
pockets.design_note: Bruiser packs on the lower terrace; ~40 cells each because hounds come in assist packs and need room to be kited round the den.

pockets.name: Jadewing Galleries
pockets.design_note: The main moth farm on the middle terrace: the terrace walls above and below cut line of sight, so ranged moths must be pulled along the shelf.

pockets.name: Sap Lifts
pockets.design_note: Moths alone on the upper terrace among the old lift-rails: the rails break line of sight, so the ranged pack must be pulled round them.

pockets.name: Vine Terrace
pockets.design_note: Lv23 hound packs mid-band on the top terrace, where the road leaves for Graftwood: a second assist den, ~40 cells each to kite round.

pockets.name: Trellis Rows
pockets.design_note: The signature construct horde: fence rows (open at both ends) channel a Vinecrawler train into lanes, ideal for cones and lines.

pockets.name: Grafting Yard
pockets.design_note: Vinecrawlers still crawl round the stalled engine they once served: a construct train that has to be kited round a central obstacle.

pockets.name: Stockwood
pockets.design_note: Vinecrawlers in the south-west woods among old graft-stock: the trees break up the train, a quieter farm for players arriving at the bottom of the band.

pockets.name: Overgrown Graft
pockets.design_note: Vinecrawlers in a run-wild corner beside the south road: a small, dense construct pocket, the last stop before Vineworks.

pockets.name: Press Terraces
pockets.design_note: Tenders alone on their own terraces at the bottom of the band: low damage, assist pulls, a calm place to learn their 5-cell spray.

pockets.name: Hare Terraces
pockets.design_note: Mid-band flee swarm: the terraces are fenced on the west and north by forest, so fleeing hares pile into the corner for a clean AoE.

pockets.name: Tender Conduits
pockets.design_note: Tenders along the conduit wall at the bottom of the band: the wall stops the assist pack spreading, so one pull is a line you can sweep.

pockets.name: Pump Warren
pockets.design_note: A few Thistlehares round the waterwheel pump: sparse (~40 cells each) and quick to bolt, so the pump and wheel are the corners to trap them against.

pockets.name: Sentinel Roots
pockets.design_note: The region's main Root Sentinel farm at mid-band: slow, aggressive and thick, so a 30+ train walks into one big Sundering Pulse.

pockets.name: Root Burrows
pockets.design_note: Sentinels in soft ground between the elder roots: a second slow, thick horde with room to gather a train, nearer the camp than the ridges.

pockets.name: Spore Drift
pockets.design_note: Sentinels next to the descent to the Basin, where the Engine's spores have drifted up: the last Sentinel train before the next field.

pockets.name: Engine Glade
pockets.design_note: Four Lv34 elites in an open glade under the root ridge: room to circle a charging stag. Slow respawn so the glade is a hunt, not a farm.

pockets.name: Bloat Fields
pockets.design_note: The Basin's signature horde: 40 slow aggressive bloats on open ground under the vents, sized for 50+ trains with quick refill.

pockets.name: Obelisk Ring
pockets.design_note: Bloats round the obelisk in a wide pocket: the obelisk splits the train, so drag them round it into one stack before the AoE.

pockets.name: Pool Drift
pockets.design_note: Bloats by the spore pool: a smaller, quieter farm away from the main field for players at the bottom of the band.

pockets.name: Engine Vents
pockets.design_note: Bloats crowding the Engine's vents beside the mouth: a narrow strip that packs a train tight, the last farm before the dungeon.

pockets.name: Sap Conduits
pockets.design_note: The densest Matron nest in the region (~12 cells each) in a round cavern you can circle; assist supports spitting from 5 cells, so pull them into a stack.

pockets.name: Piston Hall
pockets.design_note: Assist constructs round the central piston: one pull is the hall, a 30-construct fight at mid-band.

pockets.name: Spore Lung
pockets.design_note: Matrons in a side cavern off the main hall: a smaller assist pull, quieter and closer to the landing.

pockets.name: Heart Chamber
pockets.design_note: Region boss, 5-7 minute respawn, alone in its chamber.

pockets.name: Coil Dunes
pockets.design_note: Passive Sandcoils on open dunes beside the camp, at the bottom of the band: ~28 cells each, room to gather 40 with Anchor Shout.

pockets.name: Jackal Draw
pockets.design_note: Jackals den round the oasis (the water takes ~8% of the rect); assist packs come in from all sides of the water.

pockets.name: Mesa Glass
pockets.design_note: More passive Sandcoils basking on the lightning-glass below the mesa, off the main trail: a quieter second gathering ground away from the camp.

pockets.name: Buried Pipeline
pockets.design_note: Sandcoils sleeping on the warm pipe with jackals hunting them, astride the trail north: a mixed passive/assist pack.

pockets.name: Kite Heights
pockets.design_note: Ranged kites mid-band round the survey tower, ~37 cells each so a player can break line and pull them in a few at a time.

pockets.name: Scarab Wash
pockets.design_note: The main Scarab farm in a dry wash: aggressive, dense, quick refill — the Verge's horde for 30+ trains.

pockets.name: Kite Checkpoint
pockets.design_note: Aggressive ranged kites over the old checkpoint between the two camps: break line on the ruined walls and pull them in a few at a time.

pockets.name: Serai Scarabs
pockets.design_note: Lv30 scarabs near the bottom of the band west of the serai: a smaller aggressive swarm for players arriving from the Dunes.

pockets.name: Basilisk Glare
pockets.design_note: Assist bruisers at mid-band on the open glass east of the crossroads; ~30 cells each so packs can be kited round the crystal outcrop.

pockets.name: Sentry Field
pockets.design_note: The signature construct horde of the Flats: slow aggressive Sentries in a wide open corner, made for 30+ trains.

pockets.name: Heliograph Mirrors
pockets.design_note: Lv35 Sentries with Lv37 basilisks among the mirror towers mid-band: slow constructs and assist bruisers, so pull round the towers to split the pack.

pockets.name: Glass Scar
pockets.design_note: Mixed constructs and bruisers near the camp: a heavier pack for the top of the band.

pockets.name: Dial Face
pockets.design_note: Acolytes tending Wardens round the gnomon: the stone ring and gnomon split the pack, so the supports must be hunted inside it.

pockets.name: Acolyte Sands
pockets.design_note: Lv39 assist Acolytes mid-band on open sand with no Wardens to hide behind: the main support farm for new arrivals.

pockets.name: Warden Causeway
pockets.design_note: Lv42 Wardens at the top of the band on the east approach: hard-hitting constructs in smaller numbers (~48 cells each).

pockets.name: Sentry Graveyard
pockets.design_note: Lv39 Acolytes among grave markers, mending broken sentries that never rise: an easier assist farm south of the camp.

pockets.name: Strider Canal
pockets.design_note: The signature flee swarm mid-band, straddling the canal (~12% water): fleeing Striders run along the channel walls, so herd them down its length.

pockets.name: North Piers
pockets.design_note: Lv44 Striders mid-band round the aqueduct's head beside the bridge from camp: pin the fleeing swarm against the piers.

pockets.name: South Sluice
pockets.design_note: Striders in the dry south sluices: the sluice walls stop the fleeing swarm scattering, so herd them into the corners.

pockets.name: Old Cistern
pockets.design_note: Striders round the cistern by the south road: a fast, low-threat fleeing pack, easy to pin against the cistern rim.

pockets.name: Revenant Road
pockets.design_note: The Causeway's signature horde mid-band, on and beside the road: fast aggressive Revenants that form 40+ trains along the paving.

pockets.name: Seep Sinks
pockets.design_note: Lv50 Lens-drones at the top of the band round the seep pools in the west: a 7-cell ranged pocket, pulled out of line of sight so they bunch up.

pockets.name: Colossus Bed
pockets.design_note: Three Lv49 elites in open sand off the side road: slow giants with room to kite. Slow respawn makes them a hunt, and the Key Prism quest needs two.

pockets.name: Lens Array
pockets.design_note: Lv50 Lens-drones (top of band) with Revenant escorts in a long strip before the Vault door: a 7-cell ranged threat that must be pulled behind the collapsed span.

pockets.name: Mirror Gallery
pockets.design_note: The densest pocket (~10 cells each): assist Mirrorguards shoulder to shoulder among the mirrors; a round hall to circle while AoE does the work.

pockets.name: Lens Foundry
pockets.design_note: Assist constructs round the focusing engine: one pull is the foundry, a 30-construct fight at the top of the band.

pockets.name: Shaft of Noon
pockets.design_note: Assist Mirrorguards in the light-shaft: one pull brings the whole shaft, so drag them into the corridor where they bunch up.

pockets.name: Heliostat Core
pockets.design_note: Region boss, 5-7 minute respawn, alone under the heliostat.

pockets.name: Tidepool Flats
pockets.design_note: Passive Tidehoppers on the sand between the lagoon and the surf: a dense (~14 cells each) but harmless herd to re-learn AoE pulls on arrival in the region.

pockets.name: Gull Cliffs
pockets.design_note: The aggressive flock nests under the north cliffs, away from the road but within sight of the camp: players choose when to pull it.

pockets.name: Wrack Line
pockets.design_note: Coral Claw bruisers on the east beach at the top of the band (Lv40); the seaweed rocks break their line so they arrive in twos and threes.

pockets.name: Beached Pump-Buoy
pockets.design_note: Gulls perch on the stranded buoy while hoppers shelter in its shadow: an aggressive flock drags passive hoppers into the fight.

pockets.name: Polyp Gardens
pockets.design_note: Ranged Polyp Spitters among tall coral heads on the east reef: the heads break line of sight, so players pull spitters round them into melee.

pockets.name: Kelp Shallows
pockets.design_note: Polyp Spitters (Lv42) spread through the north-west shallows: the kelp screens their line of sight, so players learn to pull ranged fire out into the open.

pockets.name: West Reef
pockets.design_note: Polyp Spitters on the old crab burrows near the camp: aggressive ranged fire a short run from safety, for players who arrive at 39.

pockets.name: Dead Coral Heads
pockets.design_note: Polyp Spitters crowded on the north reef's dead coral heads: a dense ranged pack with little cover, so players must close the gap fast.

pockets.name: Pumpworks
pockets.design_note: Brine Automatons round the pump house: constructs need room (~33 cells each) and the pump blocks the middle, so packs come round both sides.

pockets.name: Kelp Beds
pockets.design_note: Kelp Tenders among the west pools, straddling the rim road: assist means a careless walk pulls the bed, and supports heal each other, so focus fire matters.

pockets.name: Barnacle Paddles
pockets.design_note: Kelp Tenders (Lv44) grown over the east tidewheels' paddles; the bay at their back means they can only be approached from the land side, and assist pulls the whole bed at once.

pockets.name: Old Pilings
pockets.design_note: Brine Automatons patching the old quay timbers near the reef-road camp: a smaller construct pocket than the pumpworks, a second Aetherite source for players arriving from the reef.

pockets.name: Hulk Graveyard
pockets.design_note: The signature horde: 40 assisting Hullborers among hull ribs, ~23 cells each. Assist empties a wreck at once; respawn is quick so the graveyard refills between trains.

pockets.name: Sunken Freighter
pockets.design_note: Hullborers riddling the half-sunk freighter: a smaller assist swarm that boils out of the hull, away from the graveyard's crowds.

pockets.name: Buoy Line
pockets.design_note: Hullborers in the timber floats of the relay buoys on the seaward bar; their shared tunnels (assist) make the whole line answer one pull.

pockets.name: Drift Bar
pockets.design_note: West of the channel, close to camp: a quieter Hullborer pocket in the driftwood for small groups.

pockets.name: Pearl Beds
pockets.design_note: Fleeing skates among oyster pools: the pools pen them in, so a player who herds from the open side gets them bunched for an AoE.

pockets.name: Relay Mast
pockets.design_note: Relay Guardians (Lv52, low end of the band) guard the mast: the construct farm of the flats and a steady Aetherite source.

pockets.name: South Strand
pockets.design_note: Relay Guardians (Lv52) walking the buoy cables on the south strand, tucked against the mangroves so a pull comes from one direction; shared sonar (assist) wakes the whole cable.

pockets.name: Stilt Ruins
pockets.design_note: Skates (Lv53) buried in the mud under the stilt houses: fleeing targets that scatter through the pilings, an easy herding pocket next to the arrival camp.

pockets.name: Lightning Masts
pockets.design_note: Aggressive ranged rays circling the masts: the masts block, so players fight among them and pull rays into melee range one ring at a time.

pockets.name: Intake Vents
pockets.design_note: Thunderhull Turtles (Lv56) basking in the warm vent outflow beside the hatch camp: assist means the vent herd moves as one, a tanky last stop before going down.

pockets.name: Ruined Breakwater
pockets.design_note: Turtle herd (Lv56, low end) in the lee of the breakwater, the sea at their backs: assist means the herd moves as one.

pockets.name: Storm Flats
pockets.design_note: Storm-wrack mix of rays and turtles round the storm pool: ranged and bruiser behaviours in one pull, the region's final mixed-AI test.

pockets.name: Pressure Hall
pockets.design_note: The densest drone nest (~12 cells each) in a round hall players can kite around: the dungeon's main AoE farm.

pockets.name: Flooded Gallery
pockets.design_note: Medusae over a flooded floor: supports alone are slow to kill but safe, a breather between drone pulls.

pockets.name: Pump Ring
pockets.design_note: Drones shielded by medusae on the way to the boss: the real test of focusing supports first.

pockets.name: Sonar Chamber
pockets.design_note: Region boss, 5-7 minute respawn, alone in its chamber.

pockets.name: Thaw Strip
pockets.design_note: Passive mites packed along the heat pipes (~19 cells each), close to the arrival camp: the warm-up herd for players arriving from Thalassia.

pockets.name: Snowfield
pockets.design_note: Open snow bounded by the north forest edge: fleeing hares run into the trees and bunch there.

pockets.name: Frozen Lake
pockets.design_note: Ranged wisps at the top of the band (Lv50) over the ice; the open water in the middle breaks their line, so players pull them round the shore.

pockets.name: Survey Line
pockets.design_note: Mites and hares among the survey ruins on the way north: a quieter mixed pocket of passive and fleeing monsters.

pockets.name: Ram Terraces
pockets.design_note: Assisting ram flocks on the south terraces, mid-band (Lv52): the region's first bruiser pack, best pulled whole and burned with AoE.

pockets.name: Glass Spines
pockets.design_note: Assisting rams among crystal spines, mid-band (Lv52); the spines split the flock into small groups, so players pull them a few at a time.

pockets.name: Windscour
pockets.design_note: Rams (Lv52) in a narrow strip between the west cliff and the road: the assisting flock charges as one and pins itself against the cliff.

pockets.name: Obelisk Field
pockets.design_note: Assisting rams sheltering round the obelisks near the east exit: the last flock before Snowcoil, pulled whole between the stones.

pockets.name: Coil Trenches
pockets.design_note: The signature horde: 40 aggressive serpents in trenches between frozen coils. The coils split the pocket into lanes that funnel a train into lines; quick respawn refills it.

pockets.name: Pumphouse Yard
pockets.design_note: Icegears at the low end of the band in the old pump yard: constructs at ~40 cells each, a steady Aetherite farm.

pockets.name: Lower Slopes
pockets.design_note: Icegears (Lv55, low end) wandering the south slopes near the lift: aggressive constructs on open ground, an easier Aetherite farm for players who took the lift up early.

pockets.name: Research Huts
pockets.design_note: Serpents and gear walkers among abandoned huts: crates and walls break the ground into rooms, a mixed swarm-plus-construct pull.

pockets.name: Vault Hollow
pockets.design_note: The pass's horde: assisting keepers (Lv62, top of the band) packed in a hollow below the road, ~22 cells each; one pull wakes the hollow, and the south cliff pins the train.

pockets.name: Vault Doors
pockets.design_note: Keepers at the top of the band guard the sealed doors; assist means the whole facade answers one pull.

pockets.name: Plough Road
pockets.design_note: Keepers (Lv62) strung along the plough route near the arrival camp: assist means a careless pull from the road brings the whole line.

pockets.name: Plough Shed
pockets.design_note: The region's elite: two Glacier Juggernauts on a 2-3 minute respawn, slow enough to kite round the shed; worth a group pull for the Aetherite.

pockets.name: Mirror Field
pockets.design_note: Mirrorshades alone on the polished centre: supports that heal each other, so the pocket teaches burst AoE over steady damage.

pockets.name: Lens Islands
pockets.design_note: Mirrorshades (Lv64, mid-band) on the lens islands among rocks, ~38 cells each: supports that mend each other, so players burst them an island at a time.

pockets.name: Lakeshore Grazing
pockets.design_note: Passive Behemoths at the top of the band on the south shore: players gather them with taunts at their own pace.

pockets.name: Shatter Line
pockets.design_note: Mirrorshades healing grazers along an open lead: the support-first lesson in a real mixed pack.

pockets.name: Haunted Drifts
pockets.design_note: Aggressive specters (Lv71, +1 over the band) swarming the soft snow over the warm conduit: a dense open-field AoE farm away from the Archive door.

pockets.name: Conduit Pylons
pockets.design_note: Aggressive sentries along the north arc's pylons, ~27 cells each: walking the ring here pulls them, by design.

pockets.name: West Arc
pockets.design_note: Aggressive sentries (Lv68, mid-band) on the west arc nearest the arrival camp: their lances reach 3 cells, so players close in before they pull.

pockets.name: Vent Breach
pockets.design_note: Lv71 specters (+1 over the band) leaking from the breach with sentries chasing them: the Archive's leak boiling out beside its door.

pockets.name: Cold Stacks
pockets.design_note: The Archive's main horde: 40 lancers between data-stack rows, ~18 cells each. The rows break their lines of fire and make lanes for line skills.

pockets.name: Cryo Wards
pockets.design_note: Long-range lancers in a round ward: pillars and crystal give cover, so players close in rather than trade shots.

pockets.name: Index Gallery
pockets.design_note: Lancers between index shelves on the way to the vault: the shelves block their shots, a ranged gauntlet taken shelf by shelf.

pockets.name: Curator's Vault
pockets.design_note: Region boss, 5-7 minute respawn, alone in the vault.

pockets.name: Ash Flats
pockets.design_note: Open ash with only two rock outcrops: passive Ashcrawlers at the bottom of the band, ~27 cells each, so returning players can gather a 40-pack with a taunt and test their AoE on a new region's numbers.

pockets.name: Slag Pools
pockets.design_note: Assisting bruisers round two lava pools: one hit wakes the pool, so the pocket is sized for a deliberate 10-15 bruiser pull, not a wander-through.

pockets.name: Heat-Sink Vents
pockets.design_note: Assisting Lv63 toads round the toppled heat-sink under the lava fissure: a second, larger toad pull kept off the main road so the camp-to-crossroads walk stays calm.

pockets.name: Crust Ridge
pockets.design_note: Beside the north road: a small passive grazer herd on the lava crust, an easy top-up for a train on the way to Cinder Track.

pockets.name: Slag Terraces
pockets.design_note: Aggressive Lv65 imps on stepped slag south of the lava stream, next to camp: a smaller first taste of the horde before the bridge.

pockets.name: Imp Hollows
pockets.design_note: The signature horde: 40 aggressive imps (~22 cells each) between the stream and the west road; quick respawn so the hollow refills between 30-mob trains.

pockets.name: Scorch Scree
pockets.design_note: Aggressive imps on the open scree under the lava falls: packs rush down on anyone climbing the east road, so trains build themselves.

pockets.name: Rail Trestles
pockets.design_note: Rail pipes break the ground into lanes; imp packs funnel along them, good for stringing a train between the trestles.

pockets.name: Hound Kennels
pockets.design_note: The main horde: 40 fast hounds in the open kennel yard. They are the quickest monster in the region, so the yard is wide (~29 cells each) to give room to kite into a stack.

pockets.name: Cold Forges
pockets.design_note: Tenders weld the hounds they live with and flee when hit: the pocket teaches killing the support first. Forge machinery splits the yard into lanes.

pockets.name: Channel Bank
pockets.design_note: Aggressive hounds along the bank between two lava channels: a long thin pocket that strings the fast packs out along the lava, an overflow for the kennels.

pockets.name: Slag Heaps
pockets.design_note: South of the channel near camp: fleeing tenders scavenging on their own, a quieter farm for Tender materials (the focus-tonic recipe).

pockets.name: The Vent Pool
pockets.design_note: The signature horde: 40 durable skinks circling the magma pool. The pool in the middle means a train loops round it naturally; crystal outcrops break line of sight.

pockets.name: Southern Fissure
pockets.design_note: Ranged worms along the fissure: the lava sits between them and the road, so players must path round and pull them off the edge.

pockets.name: Heat-Tap Ridge
pockets.design_note: Skinks and ranged Spitters mixed round the drill: the skinks rush while the worms spit from behind the machinery, the hardest pocket on the map.

pockets.name: Ash Wash
pockets.design_note: Skinks alone in the western gully, away from the Spitters: the catch-up pocket for players arriving under-levelled.

pockets.name: Girder Fields
pockets.design_note: The signature horde across the river: 40 assisting scraplings, so one hit rings the whole heap into a 30-40 train. Crates and gear scrap give a few corners to gather against.

pockets.name: Truss Graveyard
pockets.design_note: Furnace Knights in their own ground: aggressive constructs among fallen trusses, ~40 cells each so they come in twos and threes, never all at once.

pockets.name: Lava Banks
pockets.design_note: Lv77 knights patrolling the east bank above the High Span road: aggressive constructs spread along the ledge, so they come one or two at a time.

pockets.name: Lower Span Approach
pockets.design_note: Assisting scraplings by the southern bridge: one ring pulls the heap round the corner of the span, a smaller overflow for the Girder Fields.

pockets.name: Pour Channels
pockets.design_note: Lv85 wraiths (top of band) between the channel and the ring road: fragile but hard-hitting, so packs die fast and refill fast.

pockets.name: Scrap Moraine
pockets.design_note: Lv83 brutes packed on the scrap heap by the west channel: aggressive bruisers in the open, a steadier fight than the yard's aisles for players just arrived from Ironfall.

pockets.name: Mould Yard
pockets.design_note: Aggressive bruisers among the mould rows: the moulds split the yard into aisles, so Brutes come one aisle at a time.

pockets.name: Crucible Rim
pockets.design_note: Wraiths and Brutes mixed below the ring road: fast-dying hitters behind a bruiser wall, the last field test before Furnace Zero.

pockets.name: Pour Gallery
pockets.design_note: The dungeon's main farm: 40 assisting stokers in an oval hall you can circle round the pour pit; one pull wakes the gallery, the densest construct horde in Emberfall.

pockets.name: Coal Pens
pockets.design_note: Assisting Lv88 stokers on the short route to the core: they answer as one, so clear the pens or go round through the halls.

pockets.name: Stoker Halls
pockets.design_note: Assisting constructs at the cap: one pull is the whole hall. The best Living Ember and Aetherite source in the region.

pockets.name: The Zero Core
pockets.design_note: Region boss, 5-7 minute respawn; two approaches (pens or halls) so a party can choose its fight on the way in.

pockets.name: Wisp Boulevard
pockets.design_note: Open boulevard of passive wisps (~25 cells each): the safe first horde of the endgame, gathered with a taunt.

pockets.name: The Underpass
pockets.design_note: Assisting scavengers between two tower stumps: one squeal pulls the underpass, so it is sized for a 20-30 train with walls on two sides to stack against.

pockets.name: Overpass Fall
pockets.design_note: Passive wisps drifting along the fallen overpass by the west road: a quieter second boulevard, gathered with a taunt well away from the lurk packs.

pockets.name: Conduit Square
pockets.design_note: Lurks hunt among the wisps under the obelisk: assisting scavengers drag passive wisps into a fight, the mixed-AI lesson of the region.

pockets.name: Nullbloom Beds
pockets.design_note: Rooted supports in fenced beds: they barely move, so the beds are a static AoE farm. Sized at ~33 cells each so a cone clears a row at a time.

pockets.name: Dead Pond
pockets.design_note: Haulers on the boardwalk shore: aggressive bruisers on an open loop round the water, met one or two at a time.

pockets.name: Black Glasshouses
pockets.design_note: Blooms shade each other in packs: burn a row before the next one wakes. Glass and crystal break the hall into aisles.

pockets.name: Promenade
pockets.design_note: Haulers run a loop round the grey copse: aggressive bruisers that come one at a time round the trees.

pockets.name: Coupler Sidings
pockets.design_note: The signature horde: 40 assisting mite crews in the open sidings (~30 cells each); one pull is the yard, a 30-40 train for the big AoE.

pockets.name: Stalled Line
pockets.design_note: Assisting mite crews on the stalled line behind the signal tower: a smaller yard next to the camp, one crew to a pull.

pockets.name: Signal Gantries
pockets.design_note: Ranged drones among stalled carriages: the carriages block their line of fire, so players break LOS and pull them in.

pockets.name: Junction Pit
pockets.design_note: A long narrow strip at the yard's east end: mites rush along it while drones fire down its length, a corridor fight.

pockets.name: Riftside
pockets.design_note: The signature horde on the south bank where the tear is widest: 40 aggressive Riftlings with the chasm at their back, so trains are pulled south, away from the edge.

pockets.name: Tilted Blocks
pockets.design_note: Riftlings on the north bank by the Array road: a smaller pack away from the tear, a breather between Riftside trains.

pockets.name: Leaning Spires
pockets.design_note: Riftlings charge down from among the spires: the spires break up the pack, so trains arrive in strings.

pockets.name: Lower Rift
pockets.design_note: A quiet south-west corner past the narrow crossing: a small Riftling pack for players who want a lighter pull.

pockets.name: Mast Field
pockets.design_note: Fleeing flocks spread through the masts: the main horde, ~30 cells each; they scatter between the pillars when hit, so line skills down the mast rows pay best.

pockets.name: Static Dishes
pockets.design_note: Fleeing flocks round the western dish: they scatter when hit and land again nearby, so cone and line skills that catch a whole flock pay best.

pockets.name: Sentinel Ring
pockets.design_note: Assisting constructs round the great dish: engage one and the ring closes. Lattice Node and Aetherite source.

pockets.name: Control Walk
pockets.design_note: Assisting sentinels pacing the control lines north of camp: engage one and the patrol closes, the ring's lesson stretched along a strip.

pockets.name: Convergence Plaza
pockets.design_note: The densest swarm in the game (Lv95) round the obelisk ring at the crossroads: every road passes through it, so the plaza is the fight.

pockets.name: Great Colonnade
pockets.design_note: Aggressive glyph swarms between the columns: the columns split them into lanes, so the colonnade is fought one lane at a time.

pockets.name: Executor Court
pockets.design_note: Six elites round the violet crystal: the Keysigil quest's target, fought one or two at a time.

pockets.name: Lattice Verge
pockets.design_note: Glyph swarms among the rune stones in the south-west: a smaller swarm farm off the plaza, and the last stop before the Heart.

pockets.name: Lattice Conduits
pockets.design_note: The dungeon's main farm: 40 ranged Weavers in an oval chamber; circle the crystal to break their line of fire and pull them together.

pockets.name: The Loom
pockets.design_note: A hall of ranged Weavers on the short route to the chamber: line of sight is long, so players pull them back into the corridor.

pockets.name: Spindle Hall
pockets.design_note: Weavers in a long machine hall on the far route to the chamber: pull them round the machines to close the range. The best Lattice Node farm.

pockets.name: Sovereign's Chamber
pockets.design_note: The final boss, 5-7 minute respawn; reached from the loom or the hall.
